To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DPCR of ovalbumin sensitized guinea pig trachea consists of two phases: a fast and a tonic phase.
the double phase contraction of antigen-challenged tracheal strips from sensitized guinea pigs is mediated by substance P.
substance P (SP), a sensory neuropeptide, is involved in the antigen-induced contraction of guinea pig airways, especially in the second phase of the double phase contraction response.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DPCR in guinea pigs is not only a neural but also a humoral response.
SP is a major mediator in the pathogenesis in the antigen-induced contraction in guinea pig tracheal strips.
DPCR is not mediated by cholinergic nerves but by SP-containing sensory nerve fibers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DPCR is not a simple contraction, but a complicated contraction that includes the participation of the vagus nerve, the parasympathetic nervous system, SP and the sympathetic nervous system.
SP sensory nerve terminals are involved in antigen-induced bronchoconstriction.
SP sensory nerve endings in the respiratory tract are important in antigen-induced DPCR in ovalbumin-sentized guinea pigs, especially in that for TC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a model for studying the role of sensory nerve fibers in the development of antigen-induced airway hyperreactivity.
the DPCR is a complex phenomenon involving the release of a variety of mediators from the airways.
SP sensory nerve endings in the respiratory tract may play an important role, not only in the pathogenesis and the maintenance of the RC, but also in that of the TC.
